summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for post-procedural observation following his fourth transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for residual liver tumors. The procedure was performed successfully under image guidance, targeting tumors in multiple liver segments using Oncozene beads. He tolerated the intervention well with no immediate complications and remained stable throughout the brief admission. His cirrhosis, diabetes, coronary disease, and other comorbidities were managed with continuation of home medications, including diuretics, antivirals, nadolol, and rifaximin. He was monitored for post-embolization syndrome but required no pain medication. Antibiotic prophylaxis was administered, with a course of oral ciprofloxacin prescribed at discharge. He was discharged home in good condition with instructions to monitor for fever or pain, continue all medications, and follow up with his liver specialist in two weeks.
